description: Renovate configuration for Thaw (Wails v2: Go backend + React/TS frontend).
Commit/PR titles use a bare `chore:` prefix because .github/workflows/pr-title-check.yml
requires a conventional type followed immediately by a colon — `chore(deps):` would fail it.
`chore:` also means routine dependency PRs do not trigger a semantic-release version bump;
security fixes deliberately use `fix:` so a patched binary actually ships (see vulnerabilityAlerts).

schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass the batching/scheduling rules and ship as a released patch.

customManagers.description: Node.js version pinned inline in actions/setup-node steps. The two pins in renovate.yml are the bot's own runtime, not the project's build toolchain — a packageRule below disables them (RE2 has no lookahead, so they cannot be excluded by pattern).
Python version pinned inline in actions/setup-python steps (dbt integration test).
Renovate's own pinned version — the bot and the config validator in renovate.yml, plus the version CONTRIBUTING.md tells contributors to validate with, so the docs cannot drift from CI.

packageRules.description: Go indirect requirements are a side effect of `go mod tidy`, not something to bump directly.
Batch all non-major Go module updates into a single PR — one CI run covers them.
Bumping the go directive/toolchain changes every CI job (go-version-file: go.mod) — decide it manually.
Wails upgrades need `wails generate module` plus a build check on macOS, Windows and Linux — keep them isolated.
The Snowflake driver is the core runtime dependency — keep it alone so it can be run against a live account (integration tests).
Frontend build/test tooling — covered by `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build` and vitest, so batch the non-majors.
semantic-release toolchain in the root package.json — release-only, never shipped in the binary.
React runtime and its type packages must move together — a mismatched @types/react breaks the TS build.
A React major (19+) needs Ant Design / Wails compatibility work — surface it on the dashboard first.
Ant Design and its icon package share a release cadence.
An Ant Design major touches nearly every component — approve it deliberately.
Monaco editor stack (SQL editor, notebook, YAML support).
Vite/Vitest toolchain is version-coupled — upgrade it as one unit, majors included.
TypeDoc and its markdown plugin must stay in lockstep (`make docs`).
Pin actions to commit digests (supply-chain hardening) and batch workflow updates into one PR.
Node/Python versions pinned inside workflow files — one PR, approved deliberately since they change every job.

description: renovate.yml pins Node 22 for the bot's own runtime (Renovate 41+ requires it), which is
unrelated to the Node the app builds with — move it into the Renovate group rather than the
CI-toolchain one, so the bot's version and the runtime it needs travel in the same PR.
Still tracked, and not dashboard-gated: a Renovate release that requires a newer Node must be
able to surface that bump on its own, or the self-hosted job starts failing with no PR to fix it.

packageRules.description: Renovate keeps its own self-hosted pin (.github/workflows/renovate.yml) current.

description: Regenerate THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md inside the update branch.
TestThirdPartyNoticesUpToDate (run by build-check.yml) fails any dependency PR that
leaves the notices stale, so without this every Renovate PR would need a manual
`go run scripts/gen_third_party_notices.go` commit. Only THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is
committed (fileFilters); the dist stub and node_modules stay in the workspace.
Requires self-hosted Renovate with these commands allow-listed — see .github/workflows/renovate.yml.
Matched by manager rather than by manifest path so lockfile-only updates and the monthly
lockFileMaintenance branch — which change go.sum / package-lock.json without touching go.mod
or package.json — are covered too. The root package.json (semantic-release) is a harmless
no-op: its devDependencies are not shipped, so the generator produces no diff to commit.

packageRules.description: SheetJS stopped publishing to the npm registry after 0.18.5 — updates come from their own CDN, not Renovate.
